source.catalogue: Blum Catalogue and technical manual 2024/2025, online at https://publications.blum.com/2024/catalogue/en/ (Box systems from p. 194, CLAUDE.md T78); LEGRABOX standard cabinet pages: inner drawer M en/204, inner drawer K en/208
source.read: T78 F16, 11.10.2026. From this container publications.blum.com, www.blum.com, d2.blum.com and every dealer host answer 403 to CONNECT at the egress proxy (recorded in the proxy's status, 22:26 UTC) and WebFetch cannot resolve them, so NO page was opened. Every value below was read from web-search result snippets of the named URL; `page` is the catalogue page the search index attaches to that URL. Nothing is taken from memory; a value nobody printed is null and the sentence beside it says so.
source.caveat: three kinds of value: `printed` (as the snippet of the named URL shows it), null (not found, with a note), and `derived` (arithmetic on printed values, with `how`). Every one is owner to confirm against the catalogue page itself. The catalogue's own titles use a dash between the kind and the height ('Inner drawer', dash, 'M'); this file writes a comma in its place.

arrangement.what: the Blum 'inner drawer behind a front': behind ONE front, a deep pull-out below (LEGRABOX high fronted pull-out C or F on its own cabinet profiles) and, above it in the same opening, an inner drawer (M or K) or inner pull-out (C) on its own cabinet profiles, reached when the front pull-out is open. CLAUDE.md T78 F16: a drawer row may be `double: true`; the inner drawer's box height, runner length and the clearance between the two boxes come from here.

blumPairingEvidence.printed: A locking bar set is specified for one drawer, M, and one high fronted pull-out, C, which shows that an M drawer and a C-height high-fronted pull-out are planned together in a tier (2024/2025 catalogue, the locking bar page; page number not readable from the snippet)

minimumFrontHeightRule.note: no source read prints Blum's minimum FRONT height for a deep pull-out with an inner drawer above it. The arithmetic the engine can use is the SUM of the two space requirements below (derived.stackMinimumMm); it is the engine's own until the owner confirms it against the catalogue's planning page.

stackMinimumMm.how: the SUM of the two space requirements of the pair, nothing else added: the deep pull-out below plus the inner drawer above; the engine's own `profile.baseDrawerUnit.boxTopClearance` (5) is NOT in this sum and is a separate owner's number

F_below_M_above.note: the F high fronted pull-out's space requirement in cabinet was not printed in any snippet read, so the sum cannot be formed; null until the owner reads it off the catalogue page

clearanceBetweenBoxes.note: Blum prints a space requirement per drawer (the cabinet height one drawer takes, runner included), not a gap between two boxes; the gap is inside the space requirement. The engine's `boxTopClearance` 5 is the owner's own and stays.

engineNotes.whatF16Takes: box height options: the inner drawer M (side 90.5, space 109) and K (side 128.5, space null) and the inner pull-out C (side 177, space 191); the lower box: a high fronted pull-out C (space 193) or F (space null); runner nominal lengths 270 to 650 in Blum's ladder, 450 to 600 as sold in inner drawer kits; the clearance between the boxes is inside Blum's space requirements, so the engine's `double` row needs the SUM (derived.stackMinimumMm) and refuses a front shorter than it in words.
engineNotes.ourBoxes: the engine's boxes are wooden (profile.baseDrawerUnit, drawerBox.js), not LEGRABOX; Blum's numbers here size the CATALOGUE arrangement the owner asked for ('szuflada na sztućce z bluma'); the wooden box's own height law stays the engine's.
